title: Quantification of the range of motion of the finger without and with an exoskeleton using real-time magnetic resonance imaging (real-time MRI)
summary:
The aim of this study is to observe what happens inside the finger when a button is pressed, as this is a common activity in industry. The participants have to press a button several times and hold it briefly. This movement is recorded using real-time MRI and then analyzed. In addition to the normal movement, the experiment is also carried out with an exoskeleton on the finger. The aim of the study is to compare movement without an exoskeleton with movement with an exoskeleton.
Healthy, adult test subjects without injuries or other diseases of the fingers may participate.
conditions: Hyperextension of the peripheral interphalangeal joint

interventions.name: 20 healthy test subjects (10 men, 10 women) each apply a defined pressure with thumb and index finger with and without exoskeleton.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
healthy trial participants without injuries or other diseases of the fingers
Exclusion criteria:
Participants aged <18 years, pregnant or breastfeeding women, participants with metal implants such as heart valves, pacemakers, defibrillators or other implants that prohibit an MRI examination. Participants with other metal implants, metal splinters, tattoos or significant claustrophobia. Previous operations and other injuries in the study area. Chronic illnesses such as high blood pressure or diabetes mellitus.
